## Hypothesis

We aim to verify the BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON strategy using real OPRA ticks over the last 30 days to detect slippage or execution bias compared to the paper simulation (BS-synthetic). The hypothesis is that real-fills P&L will deviate from paper simulation by less than ±20% on anchor days, indicating robust execution.

## Mechanism

Replay all triggered signals from the last 30 days using OPRA tick data. For each signal, simulate entry at mid-price with slippage model, apply chart-stop (primary invalidation) and chandelier profit-lock (trailing 0.15 off HWM), and compute actual P&L. Compare aggregate results to paper simulation (BS-synthetic) from Stage-1 run.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+ account; $1K paper ≈14% headline P&L scaling.
2. **Sample bias:** Last 30 days (approx 21 trading days); selection method = time-based window; overfit risk = high if regime-shift (e.g., volatility shift) within window.
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (no WF/OOS split performed; last 30 days is contiguous recent window).
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (OPRA tick replay not executed; requires running `kitchen_stage1_runner.py` with real-fills simulator).
5. **Failure modes:** Worst day = -$23.95 (4/29 paper sim); max drawdown = $4,701.52 (paper sim); blow-up scenario = prolonged low-VIX regime causing repeated whipsaws in ribbon entries.
6. **Concentration:** Top 5 days = 999.0% of paper sim P&L (indicating extreme concentration; requires real-fills verification).
